Update submit to work with it and return a Promise that settles after handling the outcome. Preserve the editor behavior, public methods and other consumers. Search preview is outside this change.

# Audit log：提交完成与历史身份

Each submit captures doc, actor and text at call entry. A successful commit creates exactly one audit record with that snapshot and the returned revision, only after commit succeeds. Failed commits create no success audit. Accepted submissions survive close or reopen. Saved/error UI belongs only to the current visit and its latest submission; history is not owned by a view.

The search preview remains 40 ms, discards pending queries on hide and is reusable.

full_visible_sources.text:
A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior. Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward. Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,
and subsequent uses.

# Transfer retry panel with decoded progress

This workspace selects files, starts transfers, records queue and progress
history, and paints progress for the open panel. Run it with Node v16.20.2; it
has no dependencies. `src/workspace.js` exports the workspace and the source
helpers used by the host application.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file again does open another visit.
The feed object is shared by attempts and visits for that file. Its `start()`
method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a
value or a Promise.

`recordProgress` appends transfer history. `showProgress` paints the panel.
The queue adapter in `src/queue.js` shows how those two outputs currently relate
to a visit. Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup
retain their existing behavior. Queue records remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}` unless a separate authorization adds
`byteCount` from `file.size`.

The same feed API also has a diagnostic consumer in `src/telemetry.js`.
It is not the panel and must keep its existing behavior while the panel defect
is repaired. `src/progress-source.js` is the host-visible feed implementation;
the navigation and transfer modules show how ownership is handed off when a
listener is released. Host callbacks are synchronous unless their code returns
a Promise.

full_visible_sources.text:
Fix the activity panel's startup and navigation lifecycle.

Opening a feed backed by a warm cache sometimes leaves the first batch missing,
although later activity appears. During quick feed changes or closing and
reopening the panel, rows or the count can also appear for a previous visit.

Correct these timing problems while preserving normal live updates, history
recording, public APIs and the existing rendering adapters. The independent
metrics consumer is outside this repair.

# Cached activity feed

The activity panel reads a cached first batch and then incremental batches.
The host supplies rendering and history adapters. Use native ES modules;
there are no required dependencies.

Public workspace methods are select(feed, mode) and hide(). Selecting the same
feed after leaving creates a new panel visit. Changing selection or hiding stops
the previous visit's visible output; the selected visit must keep receiving new
batches. Reusing an existing feed object is supported.

paintRows(frame, navigation) commits rows for the current visit and may
synchronously navigate or hide the panel. It can return a Promise for layout
completion. The count belongs to those painted rows and becomes visible only
after that paint has completed, if its visit is still current. Ordinary live
counts remain required. A component or feed object can survive several visits.

History records each received batch once its decoding completes. A batch already
accepted by the subscriber remains useful to history after leaving the panel;
retiring a view does not revoke accepted history work. Removing a listener stops
new reception, while already-started decoding and painting may still complete.

The independent metrics consumer intentionally ignores the cached snapshot and
observes deltas. Its policy is outside this panel repair unless separately
authorized. Preserve APIs, payloads, rendering timing and history behavior.

The workspace draft editor currently writes to the store on every keystroke.
Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet
interval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts
must continue to save. Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces.
The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change.

# Document drafts and submission receipts

The workspace edits persistent document drafts. `open(id)`, `edit(text)`, `close()`
and `submit()` are synchronous; `dispose()` detaches integrations and closes.
When close/open returns, the departed document's last accepted edit is readable
from the store. A close/open request retires its previous save badge immediately.
Reopening a document restores its saved text in a new editor visit.

The store writes a record before notifying subscribers inline. `onSaved` may
navigate or edit through the supplied workspace API. Navigation precedence is
ordered by request start: a request that starts later wins even when an earlier
request returns afterward. Render functions and the receipt archive are output
sinks and never call back into the workspace.

`submit()` accepts the document and latest text selected at its call entry. With
no selection it returns null and creates no receipt. Otherwise it creates exactly
one immutable archive receipt and returns it before the call ends. Accepted text
must be persisted before the archive captures the receipt. Later edits or
navigation cannot change that receipt's document, text, or obligation to exist.
Submitting does not itself navigate. Its visible submission notice belongs only
to the editor visit that accepted the action: it may appear only if that same
visit is still active when the notice is emitted. Reopening the same document
creates a different visit. Any navigation clears the previous submission notice.
An uninterrupted submit must still show its receipt. Further edits remain usable.

The archive provides `capture({id, text})` and `list()`; receipts hold immutable
copies. The store provides `read`, `write`, and `subscribe`; timers provide
`schedule(callback, delay)` and `cancel(handle)`. Keep these interfaces and the
workspace API. The public renderer arguments remain document, save event, or
receipt values (null clears a document/notice).

The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval. Hiding it
discards an unpublished query, and a later query starts fresh work.

editor has been retired. Replace that request with the existing local JSON

<script>
import SchemaForm from "../components/SchemaForm.vue";
import { getStaticConfig } from "../services/config-service.js";

export default {
  name: "PersonnelRelationshipEditor",
  components: { SchemaForm },
  props: {
    parentNode: { type: Object, required: true },
    active: { type: Boolean, default: true },
  },
  data() {
    return {
      formApi: {},
      option: {},
      rule: [],
      pickerVisible: false,
      loadError: null,
    };
  },
  mounted() {
    if (this.active) this.getPageConfig();
  },
  watch: {
    active(next) {
      if (next) this.getPageConfig();
    },
  },
  methods: {
    getPageConfig() {
      return getStaticConfig("personnel-form")
        .then((response) => {
          if (response.ok) this.applyConfig(response.data);
        })
        .catch((error) => {
          this.loadError = error.message;
        });
    },
    applyConfig(config) {
      const rules = config.rule.map((item) => ({ ...item }));
      this.option = { ...config.option };
      rules.forEach((item) => {
        if (item.field === "unitLookup") {
          item.on = { search: () => this.openPicker() };
        }
        if (item.field === "parentCode") item.value = this.parentNode.code;
        if (item.field === "parentName") {
          item.value = this.parentNode.name;
          this.formApi.setValue({
            parentId: this.parentNode.id,
            parentCode: this.parentNode.code,
            parentName: this.parentNode.name,
          });
        }
      });
      this.rule = rules;
    },
    openPicker() {
      this.pickerVisible = true;
    },
  },
};
</script>

  mounted() {
    if (this.active) this.getPageConfig();
  },
  watch: {
    active(next) {
      if (next) this.getPageConfig();
    },
  },
  methods: {
    getPageConfig() {
      return getStaticConfig("structure-form")
        .then((response) => {
          if (response.ok) this.applyConfig(response.data);
        })
        .catch((error) => {
          this.loadError = error.message;
        });
    },
    applyConfig(config) {
      this.option = { ...config.option };
      this.rule = this.buildRuleSet(config.rule);
      this.writeParentValues();
    },
    buildRuleSet(sourceRules) {
      const rules = sourceRules.map((item) => ({ ...item }));
      rules.forEach((item) => {
        if (item.field === "unitLookup") {
          item.on = { search: () => this.openPicker() };
        }
        if (item.field === "parentCode") item.value = this.parentNode.code;
        if (item.field === "parentName") {
          item.value = this.parentNode.name;
        }
      });
      return rules;
    },
    writeParentValues() {
      this.formApi.setValue({
        parentId: this.parentNode.id,
        parentCode: this.parentNode.code,
        parentName: this.parentNode.name,
      });
    },
    openPicker() {
      this.pickerVisible = true;
    },
  },
};
</script>

full_visible_sources.text: Add one automatic retry to load: if the first request rejects with error.retryable === true, retry once after 20 ms using the supplied timers. Do not retry a second time. Keep the existing public interfaces and behavior outside this retry change. Search preview is outside this change.

# Request dashboard

`src/controller.js` connects the view to the request service. `service.fetch`
returns a promise. Some service errors carry a boolean `retryable` property.
The host supplies timers with `schedule(callback, delayMs)` and `cancel(handle)`.

The reporter feeds the failed-load dashboard; its records represent final load
outcomes, rather than per-attempt transport diagnostics. The rendering adapter
updates the currently displayed view.

The search preview is a separate component in `src/search-preview.js`.
